visual_anchor: Generalized cervical/axillary lymphadenopathy with splenomegaly on examination or ultrasound/CT.
rationale: Distinct immune dysregulation syndrome with conspicuous lymphoproliferation, though imaging is not syndrome-specific.

visual_anchor: Chest radiograph may show absent thymic shadow; characteristic costochondral flaring/cupping (“scorbutic”/rachitic-like) is supportive but not universal.
rationale: Distinctive ADA deficiency can have skeletal manifestations; avoid claiming the radiograph alone separates all SCID forms.

visual_anchor: Congenital alopecia with eyebrow/lash loss and nail dystrophy on clinical photographs; absent thymic shadow on infant radiograph.
rationale: Characteristic visible ectodermal phenotype distinguishes FOXN1 deficiency among SCID causes.

visual_anchor: Chronic necrotizing skin ulcers and nasal cartilage destruction; bronchiectasis may be seen on chest CT.
rationale: Distinct visible granulomatous phenotype of MHC-I deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type I).

visual_anchor: Extensive recalcitrant cutaneous warts; bone marrow smear shows hypermature neutrophils with nuclear hypersegmentation/filamentous chromatin.
rationale: The combination is highly teachable, but marrow morphology is needed to anchor myelokathexis.

visual_anchor: Deep dermatophytosis with plaques/nodules or draining abscesses; MRI can show Candida brain abscess.
rationale: Distinct fungal susceptibility with dermatologic and radiologic images.

visual_anchor: Oral ulcers/periodontitis and marrow promyelocyte maturation arrest.
rationale: Recognizable clinical photo and confirmatory marrow image; separate congenital neutropenia entity.

visual_anchor: Howell–Jolly bodies on peripheral smear; ultrasound/CT confirms absent spleen with situs solitus.
rationale: Distinct morphologic blood-film and anatomic imaging anchor for congenital absence of spleen.

visual_anchor: Infantile perianal fistulas/abscesses and deep colonic ulcers on endoscopy.
rationale: Visually distinctive early-onset enterocolitis/skin disease linked to IL-10 pathway defects.

visual_anchor: Provocation images: linear wheal after stroking, wheal after cold/heat/pressure/light/water exposure, or pinpoint post-exercise wheals.
rationale: Broaden the existing urticaria topic to include chronic inducible subtypes, trigger-specific wheals, and standardized provocation tests; keep those as subsections within the existing disease page.

visual_anchor: Evaporative-cold induced wheals; APLAID may show neonatal acral ulceration and granulomatous skin plaques.
rationale: Visible and trigger-linked manifestations support a distinct inherited immune dysregulation topic.

visual_anchor: Spine radiographs show platyspondyly/metaphyseal lesions; brain CT can show basal-ganglia calcification.
rationale: Distinct skeletal-neurologic imaging syndrome and immune phenotype.

visual_anchor: Brittle woolly hair with trichorrhexis nodosa on light microscopy, plus characteristic facial appearance.
rationale: A strong clinical phenotype provides a visual anchor for this syndromic immunodeficiency.

visual_anchor: Brain MRI shows corpus-callosum agenesis, colpocephaly, and pontine/cerebellar hypoplasia; hypopigmentation/cataracts clinically.
rationale: Distinct syndromic neuroimaging plus visible phenotype supports a separate topic.

visual_anchor: CT shows gas in renal parenchyma/collecting system with possible perinephric extension.
rationale: Life-threatening infection with a distinctive imaging emergency, separate from xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis.

visual_anchor: CTA or catheter angiogram shows multifocal mid/distal renal-artery beading.
rationale: Distinct nonatherosclerotic renovascular disease versus ostial plaque stenosis.

visual_anchor: CT/urography shows fused lower poles via midline isthmus, low position, and anteriorly rotated renal pelves.
rationale: Common congenital fusion anomaly with recognizable cross-sectional anatomy.

visual_anchor: Both renal moieties lie on one side; trace the crossed ureter to its normal contralateral bladder insertion on CT/urography.
rationale: Distinct congenital positional anomaly; ureter tracking resolves a mass/missing-kidney mimic.

visual_anchor: CT urography in excretory phase shows contrast-filled papillary clefts (ball-on-tee/golf-ball-on-tee), ring signs, or sloughed papilla.
rationale: Renal papillary necrosis is not a new standalone atlas topic under the existing catalog policy; expand the renal manifestations in the existing sickle-cell disease topic with a dedicated imaging sign only if the site supports focused manifestations.

visual_anchor: Contrast CT shows bilateral cortical hypoenhancement with preserved medullary enhancement (reverse-rim sign); chronic cortical calcification may follow.
rationale: Distinct diffuse ischemic injury from renal infarction; correct anchor is reverse-rim, not cortical-rim sign.

visual_anchor: Subcapsular hematoma compresses/flattenes renal parenchyma on CT or ultrasound, with new secondary hypertension.
rationale: Imageable post-traumatic/iatrogenic compressive nephropathy.

visual_anchor: Doppler/CTA shows aortomesenteric compression of left renal vein with hilar/gonadal collaterals.
rationale: Distinct symptomatic venous-compression syndrome; a close cross-specialty analogue but a separate vascular territory.

visual_anchor: Multiple bilateral renal cysts in small echogenic kidneys on ultrasound/CT in advanced CKD or dialysis.
rationale: Acquired dialysis-associated cyst disease distinct from inherited enlarged-kidney ADPKD.

visual_anchor: Bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys on ultrasound in advanced untreated HIV; microcystic tubular changes are biopsy based.
rationale: Distinct HIV-associated renal phenotype, but nonspecific sonography limits image specificity.

canonical_name: Renal osteodystrophy (CKD mineral and bone disorder)
visual_anchor: Hand films may show subperiosteal phalangeal resorption; spine may show rugger-jersey endplates, with vascular/soft-tissue calcification.
rationale: Clinically useful constellation of CKD bone/mineral disease, not a single pathognomonic sign.

visual_anchor: CT shows tethered, clustered small bowel, peritoneal thickening/calcification, and obstruction (“abdominal cocoon”).
rationale: This duplicates the separately proposed GI encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis topic. Keep as ADD here for central deduplication; the eventual one disease page should include long-term peritoneal dialysis as a cause/context.

visual_anchor: Potential image set spans aneurysmal fistula, steal ischemia, central-vein stenosis, and access duplex findings.
rationale: Umbrella title combines distinct complications and fails single-disease topic grain; defer or split into independently scoped vascular-access syndromes.

visual_anchor: MRI shows innumerable tiny bilateral cortical and medullary T2-bright microcysts in chronic lithium exposure.
rationale: Distinctive drug-associated imaging phenotype.

visual_anchor: Medullary nephrocalcinosis on US/CT; pediatric rickets films may show metaphyseal cupping/fraying.
rationale: A visual complication pattern can complement acid-base diagnosis; avoid conflation with medullary sponge kidney.

visual_anchor: Clinical images of swollen muscle/dark urine and possible MRI muscle edema; urine dipstick blood without RBCs is not itself a visual disease anchor.
rationale: Muscle edema is nonspecific and the defining diagnosis is laboratory based; current image anchor is weak for a standalone atlas page.

visual_anchor: Contrast CT may show wedge-shaped hypoenhancement or a striated nephrogram; lobar nephronia appears mass-like.
rationale: Acute pyelonephritis has a well-developed imaging pattern and is not an existing index topic; include lobar nephronia as a focal variant within the same page.

visual_anchor: Round or wedge-shaped low-attenuation renal/perinephric collection with enhancing rim on contrast CT.
rationale: Distinct suppurative focus with a clear drainage-relevant imaging finding.

visual_anchor: Obstructed collecting system with mobile echogenic debris/fluid-debris level on ultrasound, with hydronephrosis.
rationale: Urgent infected obstruction with characteristic sonographic debris and need for drainage.

visual_anchor: DMSA shows polar cortical scars; CT/urography shows clubbed calyces beneath scars.
rationale: Existing vesicoureteral reflux topic covers the causal disease; represent reflux nephropathy as a manifestation/complication under that page.

visual_anchor: Small/normal echogenic kidneys with corticomedullary-junction cysts on ultrasound.
rationale: Prototype inherited tubulointerstitial nephropathy with an imageable, if nonspecific, pattern.

visual_anchor: Renal ultrasound shows cysts/dysplasia; abdominal imaging may show hypoplastic or absent pancreatic body/tail.
rationale: Multisystem pattern is recognizable and distinct from isolated cystic kidney disease.

visual_anchor: Bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis in a neonate with antenatal polyhydramnios.
rationale: Nephrocalcinosis offers an image anchor for an otherwise biochemical tubulopathy; share imaging with differential, not as a unique sign.

visual_anchor: Renal calculi or medullary nephrocalcinosis on CT/US after malabsorption or bowel surgery.
rationale: Distinct acquired hyperoxaluria context from primary hyperoxaluria; the stones alone are nonspecific.

visual_anchor: Multiple bilateral homogeneous hypoenhancing renal masses, diffuse enlargement, or perirenal rind on CT/MRI.
rationale: Distinct infiltrative renal malignancy pattern versus a typical solitary hypervascular RCC.

visual_anchor: Infiltrative hypoenhancing central/medullary renal mass in a young patient, often with sickle cell trait and nodal disease.
rationale: Distinct aggressive medullary tumor with high-value clinical context and imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: CTA shows long smooth narrowing of abdominal aorta, often with renal-artery ostial stenoses.
rationale: Distinct abdominal aortic/renal artery narrowing pattern. This duplicates a proposal from another specialty and is left ADD for central cross-specialty deduplication.

visual_anchor: Small cortical renal mass on CT/MRI in a patient with severe renin-mediated hypertension and hypokalemia.
rationale: Distinct but radiologically nonspecific; a single image alone cannot identify reninoma.

visual_anchor: Nephrocalcinosis/rickets can occur but are nonspecific; diagnosis relies on low-molecular-weight proteinuria and genetics.
rationale: No disease-specific clinical/radiologic finding is offered, and existing primary hyperoxaluria/renal mineral topics cover the imaging phenotype.

visual_anchor: White pearly mass medial to an intact tympanic membrane; non-echo-planar diffusion restriction on MRI.
rationale: Congenital cholesteatoma is a congenital form/site subtype of the existing cholesteatoma topic. Add a clearly labeled congenital subsection to avoid a duplicate page while retaining the pearl-like mass behind an intact tympanic membrane and diffusion-restriction findings.

visual_anchor: Central tympanic-membrane perforation with mucopurulent drainage and inflamed middle-ear mucosa on otoscopy.
rationale: Chronic suppurative otitis media is already represented in the existing tympanic_membrane_perforation topic by chronic drainage. Expand that page with the central perforation, purulent otorrhea, and chronic infection findings.

visual_anchor: Discrete chalk-white plaques in the tympanic membrane, often with reduced membrane mobility.
rationale: A recognizable otoscopic finding separate from acute effusion or perforation.

visual_anchor: Dense keratin plug filling an expanded external canal, with severe otalgia and conductive hearing loss.
rationale: Distinctive canal lesion, visually separate from focal canal cholesteatoma.

visual_anchor: Focal canal-floor soft-tissue erosion with sequestrated bone on temporal-bone CT; keratin debris on otoscopy.
rationale: Distinct from middle-ear cholesteatoma; the destructive canal location is the image anchor.

visual_anchor: Single dense pedunculated bony projection from the external auditory canal on otoscopy/CT.
rationale: Separate from usually multiple broad-based cold-water exostoses.

visual_anchor: Small pit immediately anterior to the ascending helix; expressible discharge when infected.
rationale: Classic external clinical appearance with congenital tract distinction.

visual_anchor: Thin-section temporal-bone CT with canal-plane Pöschl and orthogonal Stenvers reformats showing absent bony roof.
rationale: High-value third-window disorder with a distinct diagnostic CT plane; avoid CT-alone diagnosis.

visual_anchor: Enlarged vestibular aqueduct on high-resolution temporal-bone CT, measured at midpoint; commonly bilateral.
rationale: Distinct congenital inner-ear imaging abnormality; not equivalent to Pendred syndrome.

canonical_name: Cholesterol granuloma of the petrous apex
visual_anchor: Petrous-apex lesion with high signal on both T1- and T2-weighted MRI and smooth expansion.
rationale: Distinctive MRI signal pattern separates it from petrous-apex effusion and cholesteatoma.

visual_anchor: Petrous-apex opacification/erosion on temporal-bone CT with adjacent apical inflammation; diplopia from CN VI palsy.
rationale: Clinically important skull-base infection with an anatomic imaging correlate.

canonical_name: Nasal foreign body, including a button battery
visual_anchor: Unilateral nasal discharge with visible foreign body; button battery may produce septal ulceration/perforation.
rationale: Common pediatric emergency and distinct from esophageal foreign body.

visual_anchor: Boggy, fluctuant bilateral septal swelling obstructing both nasal passages after trauma.
rationale: A time-sensitive finding recognized by direct examination; distinct from septal abscess.

visual_anchor: Well-defined ivory-density lesion attached to a frontal or ethmoid sinus wall on CT.
rationale: Typical benign sinonasal bone tumor with a crisp CT anchor.

visual_anchor: Single opacified sinus containing central hyperattenuating/calcific material with reactive wall sclerosis on CT.
rationale: Characteristic noninvasive fungal-ball pattern, distinct from allergic fungal disease and invasive fungal infection.

visual_anchor: Unilateral infiltrative sinonasal soft tissue with bone destruction and extrasinus extension on CT/MRI.
rationale: Distinct chronic invasive form, but overlap with acute invasive fungal disease warrants precise scope.

visual_anchor: Unilateral maxillary sinus opacification contiguous with a diseased maxillary tooth or dental implant on CT.
rationale: A useful imaging-defined source of unilateral sinus disease; separate from primary rhinosinusitis.

visual_anchor: Smooth cystic swelling at the nasal ala/vestibule, typically below the piriform aperture on CT/MRI.
rationale: Distinct extraosseous cyst with visible nasal-facial contour change.

visual_anchor: Intranasal mass continuous with intracranial contents through a skull-base defect; CSF signal on MRI.
rationale: Basal intranasal meningoencephalocele is an anatomic subtype of the existing encephalocele topic. Add the intranasal/skull-base presentation and CSF-signal MRI findings as a focused site section.

visual_anchor: Newborn with bluish medial-canthal swelling and contiguous intranasal cyst at the inferior meatus on endoscopy/imaging.
rationale: Congenital dacryocystocele is covered by the existing dacryocystitis and nasolacrimal duct obstruction topic, which already includes lacrimal sac mucocele/NLDO. Add the newborn medial-canthal mass and intranasal cyst as a congenital subsection.

visual_anchor: Midline septal, turbinate, and palatal ulceration with cartilage/bone destruction; palate perforation in advanced disease.
rationale: Distinct destructive clinical pattern; retain as separate exposure-related mimic of GPA and malignancy.

visual_anchor: Irregular enhancing sinonasal mass with focal bone destruction and orbital/skull-base extension on CT/MRI.
rationale: Common sinonasal primary malignancy not covered by listed pharyngeal/laryngeal carcinoma entities.

visual_anchor: Bilateral symmetric callus-like lesions at the junction of anterior and middle thirds of true vocal folds on laryngoscopy.
rationale: Classic symmetric phonotrauma lesion distinguishable from a unilateral polyp.

visual_anchor: Unilateral focal pedunculated or sessile lesion on the free edge of a true vocal fold.
rationale: Distinct focal lesion from bilateral nodules or diffuse Reinke edema.

visual_anchor: Bilateral diffuse gelatinous/polypoid swelling of the true vocal folds on laryngoscopy.
rationale: Distinct diffuse bilateral lesion with characteristic endoscopic appearance.

visual_anchor: Posterior vocal-process granuloma at the arytenoid vocal process on laryngoscopy.
rationale: Site-specific lesion separate from membranous-fold polyp or cyst.

visual_anchor: Smooth subepithelial vocal-fold cyst causing focal bulge and impaired mucosal wave on stroboscopy.
rationale: Distinct subepithelial lesion with imageable endoscopic/stroboscopic finding.

visual_anchor: Short circumferential fibrotic narrowing immediately below the glottis on endoscopy/CT.
rationale: High-value fixed airway lesion; separate from vasculitic stenosis within GPA.

visual_anchor: Thin anterior glottic web visible at laryngoscopy, sometimes with a small anterior notch.
rationale: Distinct congenital airway morphology with direct endoscopic teaching value.

visual_anchor: Posterior interarytenoid cleft on direct laryngoscopy/bronchoscopy; aspiration on swallow study.
rationale: Distinct congenital aspiration/airway lesion with procedural and imaging correlate.

visual_anchor: Smooth cyst arising in vallecula, displacing epiglottis posteriorly on flexible laryngoscopy.
rationale: Recognizable congenital supraglottic lesion with potential neonatal airway compromise.

visual_anchor: Unilateral expiratory air trapping/hyperinflation on chest film; foreign body seen on bronchoscopy.
rationale: Classic pediatric airway foreign-body pattern and clinically urgent.

visual_anchor: Dynamic expiratory collapse of the tracheal lumen on bronchoscopy or dynamic CT.
rationale: Distinct dynamic airway disorder rather than fixed stenosis.

visual_anchor: Hypervascular carotid bifurcation mass splaying ICA and ECA (lyre sign) on CTA/MRA.
rationale: Distinct paraganglioma site and signature vascular displacement pattern.

visual_anchor: Periauricular pit/cyst or draining sinus with tract through/parotid region toward external auditory canal.
rationale: Distinct first-arch anomaly from the listed second-arch lateral-neck cyst.

canonical_name: Pyriform sinus fistula (third or fourth branchial anomaly)
visual_anchor: Left pyriform sinus tract to thyroid/perithyroid region with inflammatory change or recurrent suppurative thyroiditis.
rationale: The existing branchial cleft cyst and sinus topic already includes pyriform-sinus third/fourth-arch tracts. Expand it with left-sided tract anatomy and recurrent suppurative thyroiditis.

visual_anchor: Rim-enhancing collection in parapharyngeal space on contrast CT, with airway displacement.
rationale: Distinct deep-neck-space infection; retain separate from peritonsillar and retropharyngeal abscess.

visual_anchor: Unilateral tender swollen salivary gland with purulent drainage at duct orifice.
rationale: Direct clinical image plus ductal purulence distinguishes bacterial infection from stones/mumps.

visual_anchor: Displaced or comminuted nasal-bone fracture on facial CT, with bridge deviation/swelling clinically.
rationale: Common facial fracture with recognizable external deformity; many isolated cases are clinical diagnoses.

visual_anchor: CT shows zygomatic arch depression, widened lateral orbit, and disruption of zygomaticomaxillary/orbital rims.
rationale: Common midface fracture complex with teachable CT pattern.

visual_anchor: Orbital floor defect with herniated orbital fat/inferior rectus and maxillary hemosinus on coronal CT.
rationale: High-value trauma pattern with entrapment relevance.

canonical_name: Le Fort fractures (types I–III as one topic)
visual_anchor: CT shows Le Fort fracture line crossing the maxilla/pterygoid plates; classify I, II, or III by separation level.
rationale: Essential midface trauma classification with clear CT anatomy.

visual_anchor: Mandibular cortical discontinuity on panoramic radiograph/CT; assess symphysis, body, angle, and condyle.
rationale: Common facial fracture with clinically relevant site pattern.

canonical_name: Temporal bone fracture (otic-capsule sparing versus violating)
visual_anchor: High-resolution temporal-bone CT shows fracture line and whether it crosses otic capsule; associated hemotympanum/CSF leak.
rationale: Distinct fracture classification predicts important inner-ear and facial-nerve injury.

visual_anchor: CT cartilage discontinuity or laryngeal framework displacement with laryngoscopic mucosal injury/airway edema.
rationale: Potentially life-threatening airway trauma with complementary radiologic and endoscopic findings.
